current_example.title: Example: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type

q-162327.name: Question 1
q-162327.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/d4573a2e3c7b220ac363c996c5332a3db93cc48b5b941e46a529b6912804f0c6.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z.$
q-162327.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-{y}^{2},\,\,0\le x\le 2-y-z\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8d1db6e886f00596814900ca0c4113590a37a407b65c800eb1f9926328ade50c.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-{y}^{2}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is 

$$
z=1-{y}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-z}.
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-z}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/1fe8a810a7e98c8a40739d5019ff9054a5375c0a12ae7fd1b17f8b6c8bb19f75.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

q-162327.html:
Question 1
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−y2∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then y, and then z.

a
 ∫01∫1−z1∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz
b
 ∫01∫1−z1∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz
c
 ∫01∫01−z∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz
d
 ∫01∫01−z∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz
e
 ∫01∫01∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y2,0≤x≤2−y−z}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y2}

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(z), is

z=1−y2⟹y=1−z.

and the left boundary of the region is

y=0.

Then, the type II representation of the region D is

D={(y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤1−z},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−z∫02−y−zf(x,y,z)dxdydz.
q-162327.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

q-162226.name: Question 2
q-162226.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
q-162226.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

q-162226.html:
Question 2
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0x2∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
∫01∫y2y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2,0≤z≤x2+y}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is

y=x2⟹x=y

and the right boundary of the region is

x=1.

Then, the type II representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,y≤x≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy.
q-162226.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

q-162495.name: Question 3
q-162495.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/2f95783c1e9624e58b4cd26764e94fb61d45c7aa75260ce8ca726a6c2e5db9ab.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{3-3z/2}^{3}{\int }_{8-4x/3-2z}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x.$
q-162495.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,3-\frac{3z}{2}\le x\le 3,\,\,8-\frac{4x}{3}-2z\le y\le 4\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{8-4x/3-2z}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/85d184f328ebdbed5faf2d1c43261940a8241b6637450ab5fe1c8d803026e273.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,3-\frac{3z}{2}\le x\le 3\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom  boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is 

$$
x=3-\frac{3z}{2}\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2x}{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=2.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,2-\frac{2x}{3}\le z\le 2\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/6ac58e4c98c79a1a698d052479b55a45dd2b79bed4ca11422d172fe306dac15f.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{2-2x/3}^{2}{\int }_{8-4/3x-2z}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 3

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫02∫3−3z/23∫8−4x/3−2z4f(x,y,z)dydxdz

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to y, then z, and then x.

a
 ∫03∫2−2x/32∫8−4x/3−2z4f(x,y,z)dydzdx
b
 ∫03∫02−2x/3∫8−4x/3−2z4f(x,y,z)dydzdx
c
 ∫03∫02−2x/3∫8−4x/3−2z8f(x,y,z)dydzdx
d
 ∫03∫3−x/21∫8−4x/3−2z8f(x,y,z)dydzdx
e
 ∫03∫13−x/2∫8−4x/3−2z4f(x,y,z)dydzdx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type III region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤2,3−3z2≤x≤3,8−4x3−2z≤y≤4}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)f(x,y,z)dydzdx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to y, the y-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫8−4x/3−2z4f(x,y,z)dydzdx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xz-plane:

D={(x,z):0≤z≤2,3−3z2≤x≤3}

To change the order of integration from dydxdz to dydzdx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(x), is

x=3−3z2⟹z=2−2x3

and the top boundary of the region is

z=2.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,z):0≤x≤3,2−2x3≤z≤2},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫03∫2−2x/32∫8−4/3x−2z4f(x,y,z)dydzdx.

q-162527.name: Question 4
q-162527.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
q-162527.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

q-162527.html:
Question 4
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0z3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then z, and then y.

a
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫01∫11+y∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3,1+y−z≤x≤2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(y), is

y=z3⟹z=y3

and the top boundary of the region is

z=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,y3≤z≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.
q-162527.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

q-162329.name: Question 5
q-162329.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8fc551f1439ed5a551ae8fd18234479bb062d43ae9e4faf55d896739f76e0f4d.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{4/z}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
q-162329.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 4,\,\,1\le y\le \frac{4}{z},\,\,0\le x\le 4-yz\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9a59198b60398e2b3044296c3cc76b4748785303029dccc1087320cd11cb7d55.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 4,\,\,1\le y\le \frac{4}{z}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\frac{4}{z}\,⟹\,z=\frac{4}{y}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,\,1\le z\le \frac{4}{y}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9bc88aa4f0ad07d89ff5dd3c0de16208cb8bf47d774b557a7bf2140790c95291.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{4/y}{\int }_{0}^{4-yz}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 5
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫14∫14/z∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdydz

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then z, and then y.

a
 ∫14∫14∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫14∫01/y∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫14∫01/y∫04/zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫14∫14/y∫04/zf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫14∫14/y∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):1≤z≤4,1≤y≤4z,0≤x≤4−yz}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):1≤z≤4,1≤y≤4z}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(y), is

y=4z⟹z=4y

and the bottom boundary of the region is

z=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(y,z):1≤y≤4,1≤z≤4y},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫14∫14/y∫04−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy.
q-162329.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

q-162249.name: Question 6
q-162249.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y+2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{6}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6-y}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$
q-162249.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le y\le 6,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/aa1c884900c3cb01a719dc6d22604469984d2b08291d9d925b8f37d794d455b2.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2}\}\,\cup \,\{(y,z)\,:\,2\le x\le 6,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\sqrt{y+2}\,⟹\,y={z}^{2}-2
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
z=\sqrt{6-y}\,⟹\,y=6-{z}^{2}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,{z}^{2}-2\le y\le 6-{z}^{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/e4139dde4d56e83b91e4a72d42ccdf296ad20773520ccdaa51d7a84b9e1a3f31.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-2}^{6-{z}^{2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

Question 6
?

By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to x, then y, and then z, express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

∫−22∫0y+2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy+∫26∫06−y∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

a
 ∫04∫z26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
b
 ∫02∫z2−26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
c
 ∫02∫z−26−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
d
 ∫04∫z2+16−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
e
 ∫02∫2z26+z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration R=R1∪R2, where R1 and R2 are type I regions, is given by

R1={(x,y,z):−2≤y≤2,0≤z≤y+2,−z≤x≤y2},R2={(x,y,z):2≤y≤6,0≤z≤6−y,−z≤x≤y2}.

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D consists of two type I regions in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):−2≤y≤2,0≤z≤y+2}∪{(y,z):2≤x≤6,0≤z≤6−y}.

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(z), is z=y+2⟹y=z2−2 and the right boundary of the region is z=6−y⟹y=6−z2.

Then, the type II representation of the region is

D={(y,z):0≤z≤2,z2−2≤y≤6−z2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫z2−26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

q-161524.name: Question 7
q-161524.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{z}^{2}-1}^{-z}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{-2}^{p}{\int }_{q}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{r}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$
q-161524.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(y,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,-{z}^{2}-1\le y\le -z,\,\,0\le x\le 2y+z\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-{z}^{2}-1}^{-z}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/59e5dae7cb1d621213f3e4ef792623bdfd9a42aef19c75f7ca9d65b3af32eeda.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,-{z}^{2}-1\le y\le -z\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9c968af98710367752a9d788b9b4c00d8c04e31d5494f7887ea5d2d635312338.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\,$ $z=\sqrt{-y-1}\,$ and $\,z=1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ are

$\,$ $z=0\,$ and $\,z=-y.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le -1,\,\sqrt{-y-1}\le z\le 1\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le z\le -y\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{\sqrt{-y-1}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{-y}{\int }_{0}^{2y+z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

∫01∫−z2−1−z∫02y+zdxdydz=∫−2p∫q1∫02y+zdxdzdy+∫−10∫0r∫02y+zdxdzdy

a

EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)dxdzdy+∫cd∫v3(y)v4(y)∫u3(y,z)u4(y,z)dxdzdy.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,−z2−1≤y≤−z,0≤x≤2y+z}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∫01∫−z2−1−z∫02y+zdxdydz=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫02y+zdxdzdy+∫cd∫v3(y)v4(y)∫02y+zdxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the yz-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤z≤1,−z2−1≤y≤−z}.

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we split D into two type I regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form z=z(y), are

z=−y−1 and z=1.

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form z=z(y), are

z=0 and z=−y.

So, we can write D as a union of

D1={(y,z):−2≤y≤−1,−y−1≤z≤1}

and

D2={(y,z):−1≤y≤0,0≤z≤−y}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫−2−1∫−y−11∫02y+zdxdzdy+∫−10∫0−y∫02y+zdxdzdy.
q-161524.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

q-162234.name: Question 8
q-162234.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2z}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-z}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$
q-162234.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type II regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2z,\,\,-y\le x\le z\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 3-z,\,\,-y\le x\le z\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/9b8806738b61c4ce692f555261abcd9918096a7585291954a7f11c39aadeab39.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2z\}\,\cup \,\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 3,\,0\le y\le 3-z\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

$$
y=2z\,⟹\,z=\frac{y}{2}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=3-z\,⟹\,z=3-y.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{y}{2}\le z\le 3-y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/d1a9d83672ffbd372b6a994c62771291d957e6a5c13189a6baea6d544f6a1bbc.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{3-y}{\int }_{-y}^{z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

q-162234.html:
Question 8
?

By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to x, then z, and then y, express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

∫01∫02z∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdydz+∫13∫03−z∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdydz

a
 ∫02∫y2/23−2y∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫02∫y/23−y∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫03∫y/23+y∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫03∫2y3−y∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫02∫2y2y+3∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration R=R1∪R2, where R1 and R2 are type II regions, is given by

R1={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤2z,−y≤x≤z},R2={(x,y,z):1≤z≤3,0≤y≤3−z,−y≤x≤z}.

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D consists of two type II regions in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤2z}∪{(y,z):1≤z≤3,0≤y≤3−z}.

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(y), is y=2z⟹z=y2 and the top boundary of the region is y=3−z⟹z=3−y.

Then, the type I representation of the region is

D={(y,z):0≤y≤2,y2≤z≤3−y},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫y/23−y∫−yzf(x,y,z)dxdzdy.
q-162234.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

q-162332.name: Question 9
q-162332.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-1}^{p}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{0}^{r}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$
q-162332.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(xy,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2},\,\,-2z\le x\le y+3\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/a4de9d9df51efcec67253a1c7118466f29459ffd5c9136c144d33500ec5557bc.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/18bb3e55f076e022176bb60df27d5665ed2d91d75d618969c04ce192378db922.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=\frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=4-2z.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(y,z)\,:\,-1\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le 4-2z\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-2z}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162332.html:
Question 9
?

By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

∫02∫2y−12−y/2∫−2zy+3dxdzdy=∫−1p∫0(z+1)2/2∫−2zy+3dxdydz+∫1q∫0r∫−2zy+3dxdydz

a
p=1,q=2,r=4−2z
b
 p=12,q=3,r=4−2z
c
 p=1,q=2,r=z2−4
d
 p=12,q=1,r=z2−4
e
 p=1,q=1,r=z−2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)dxdydz+∫cd∫v3(z)v4(z)∫u3(xy,z)u4(y,z)dxdydz.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤2,2y−1≤z≤2−y2,−2z≤x≤y+3}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∫02∫2y−12−y/2∫−2zy+3dxdzdy=∫ab∫v1(z)v2(x)∫−2zy+3dxdydz+∫cd∫v3(z)v4(x)∫−2zy+3dxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤y≤2,2y−1≤z≤2−y2}.

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we split D into two type II regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form y=y(z), are

y=0 and y=12(z+1)2.

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form y=y(z), are

y=0 and y=4−2z.

So, we can write D as a union of

D1={(y,z):−1≤z≤1,0≤y≤12(z+1)2}

and

D2={(y,z):1≤z≤2,0≤x≤4−2z}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫−11∫0(z+1)2/2∫−2zy+3dxdydz+∫12∫04−2z∫−2zy+3dxdydz.
q-162332.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

q-162247.name: Question 10
q-162247.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-2{x}^{3}}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{x+3}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2x}}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{x+3}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
q-162247.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,\,-2{x}^{3}\le y\le 2,\,\,-y\le z\le x+3\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,\sqrt{2x}\le y\le 2,\,\,-y\le z\le x+3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{-y}^{x+3}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/834238127fb9a55c956b2dd708e1dc7d925c63725990003eff6aac28ee42a873.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,-2{x}^{3}\le y\le 2\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\sqrt{2x}\le y\le 2\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=-2{x}^{3}\,⟹\,x=-\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
y=\sqrt{2x}\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,-\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{2}}\le x\le \frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/82bddc0c83e0e5a5824b7525bcd4fd2dc9b8f88473dfe1fd5c6cdb2ff0cefcaf.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt[3]{y/2}}^{{y}^{2}/2}{\int }_{-y}^{x+3}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

q-162247.html:
Question 10
?

By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to z, then x, and then y, express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

∫−10∫−2x32∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdydx+∫02∫2x2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdydx

a
 ∫02∫2yy2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
 ∫01∫−y32y2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
 ∫01∫2yy2/2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
 ∫02∫−y/232y∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
 ∫02∫−y/23y2/2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy.

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration R=R1∪R2, where R1 and R2 are type I regions, is given by

R1={(x,y,z):−1≤x≤0,−2x3≤y≤2,−y≤z≤x+3},R2={(x,y,z):0≤x≤2,2x≤y≤2,−y≤z≤x+3}.

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D consists of two type I regions in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):−1≤x≤0,−2x3≤y≤2}∪{(x,y):0≤x≤2,2x≤y≤2}.

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is y=−2x3⟹x=−y23 and the right boundary of the region is y=2x⟹x=12y2.

Then, the type II representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤2,−y23≤x≤12y2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫−y/23y2/2∫−yx+3f(x,y,z)dzdxdy.
q-162247.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned

q-162326.name: Question 11
q-162326.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*
q-162326.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\,0\le x\le \operatorname{cos}⁡z\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/ed7308cf6c77f5d89b94ec90237fa9161fc85429182813f38b55d916bdbdaeef.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡z.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡z\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/4fb3323b2c295df8351910890f20266840b131a4dfd8a7bba0d61a3eb03bea23.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}[\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\text{d}x]\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,[x]_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,[y]_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{3}{(1+{cos}^{2}⁡z)}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[(1+0)^{3/2}-(1+1)^{3/2}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(1-{2}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Evaluate ∫01∫arcsin⁡yπ/2∫0cos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdxdzdy.

Hint: First change the order of integration to dxdydz.

a
32+1
b
3
c
2
d
22−13
e
22
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)1+cos2⁡zdxdydz.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows: R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,arcsin⁡y≤z≤π2,0≤x≤cos⁡z}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before: ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫0cos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is type I region in the yz-plane: D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,arcsin⁡y≤z≤π2}.

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region D is y=0 and the right boundary of the region D, written in the form y=y(z), is z=arcsin⁡y⟹y=sin⁡z.

Then, the type II representation of the region is D={(y,z):0≤z≤π2,0≤y≤sin⁡z},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫01∫arcsin⁡yπ/2∫0cos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdxdzdy=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡z∫0cos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdxdydz=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡z[1+cos2⁡z∫0cos⁡zdx]dydz=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡z1+cos2⁡z[x]0cos⁡zdydz=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡zcos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdydz=∫0π/2[cos⁡z1+cos2⁡z∫0sin⁡zdy]dz=∫0π/2cos⁡z1+cos2⁡z[y]0sin⁡zdz=∫0π/2sin⁡zcos⁡z1+cos2⁡zdz=[−13(1+cos2⁡z)3/2]0π/2=−13[(1+0)3/2−(1+1)3/2]=−13(1−23/2)=22−13.

q-162253.name: Question 12
q-162253.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$*
q-162253.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {e}^{z/x}\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/e83c249a6abf9710a201462e16c646a11411dbcdbca46f34e9beb8d2db7a654b.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le 1\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

$$
x=\sqrt{z}\,⟹\,z={x}^{2}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
z=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/7e684766b85a214d1f1dd7845979052c532e11ecce74d0284b8fc379b5669957.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}[y]_{0}^{{e}^{z/x}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{e}^{z/x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{e}^{z/x}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[x{e}^{z/x}]_{z=0}^{z={x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x{e}^{x}-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[(x-1){e}^{x}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(0-\frac{1}{2})-(-1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type III region as follows: R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,z≤x≤1,0≤y≤ez/x}

Then, the type I representation of the region is D={(x,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤x2},

as shown in the diagram below.

q-162250.name: Question 13
q-162250.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$*
q-162250.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\,0\le z\le {e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/38eb7316b1ee5c947eee37a9cc10530ff08f793b7564cf0d88c6ce24e1239f9d.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/241abff7fae5d6ba3301d605ff4c4e62ff61e423515c7bc3a54b17b9aec525aa.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}[{\int }_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\text{d}z]\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}[z]_{0}^{{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}[y]_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =[-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-({e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi /2}-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡0}) \\  & =-(1-e) \\  & =e-1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162250.html:
Question 13
?

Evaluate ∫01∫arcsin⁡yπ/2∫0ecos⁡xdzdxdy.

Hint: First change the order of integration to dzdydx.

a
2e+1
b
eπ+2
c
eπ/2
d
e−1
e
4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)dzdydx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows: R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,arcsin⁡y≤x≤π2,0≤z≤ecos⁡x}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before: ∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫0ecos⁡xdzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is type II region in the xy-plane: D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,arcsin⁡y≤x≤π2}.

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is x=arcsin⁡y⟹y=sin⁡x

and the bottom boundary of the region D is y=0.

Then, the type I representation of the region is D={(x,y):0≤x≤π2,0≤y≤sin⁡x},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫01∫arcsin⁡yπ/2∫0ecos⁡xdzdxdy=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡x∫0ecos⁡xdzdydx=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡x[∫0ecos⁡xdz]dydx=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡x[z]0ecos⁡xdydx=∫0π/2∫0sin⁡xecos⁡xdydx=∫0π/2ecos⁡x[∫0sin⁡xdy]dx=∫0π/2ecos⁡x[y]0sin⁡xdx=∫0π/2ecos⁡xsin⁡xdx=[−ecos⁡x]0π/2=−(ecos⁡π/2−ecos⁡0)=−(1−e)=e−1.

q-162330.name: Question 14
q-162330.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arccos}⁡y}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*
q-162330.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{arccos}⁡y,\,\,0\le x\le 2\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/c5f4ec9b9b12411f3057bc074a14a1f541c768c30d3a9746d7a0484b0491ad2e.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{arccos}⁡y\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\operatorname{arccos}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{cos}⁡z.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{cos}⁡z\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/077fc8133673cd57aba570cca9a6e0f5f25aa742720948c46db2b9e1d05add69.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arccos}⁡y}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}[{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}y\,[x]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}2y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{y}^{2}]_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡z\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2z)\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[z+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hint: First change the order of integration to dxdydz.

a
2π
b
π4
c
4π−12
d
2
e
12

EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)ydxdydz.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows: R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤z≤arccos⁡y,0≤x≤2}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before: ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫02ydxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is type I region in the yz-plane: D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤z≤arccos⁡y}.

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region D is y=0 and the right boundary of the region D, written in the form y=y(z), is z=arccos⁡y⟹y=cos⁡z.

Then, the type II representation of the region is D={(y,z):0≤z≤π2,0≤y≤cos⁡z},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫01∫0arccos⁡y∫02ydxdzdy=∫0π/2∫0cos⁡z∫02ydxdydz=∫0π/2∫0cos⁡z[∫02ydx]dydz=∫0π/2∫0cos⁡zy[x]02dydz=∫0π/2∫0cos⁡z2ydydz=∫0π/2[∫0cos⁡z2ydy]dz=∫0π/2[y2]0cos⁡zdz=∫0π/2cos2⁡zdz=∫0π/212(1+cos⁡2z)dz=12[z+12sin⁡2z]0π/2=12(π2)=π4.

q-162334.name: Question 15
q-162334.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$*
q-162334.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡z\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3}y\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/14c67512e143995cbfcfcf9e80c8d0975bbbc42368c97aa29956bd2d3f3454a8.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡z\le y\le 1\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
z=1
$$

and the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡z\,⟹\,z={e}^{y}.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1\le z\le {e}^{y}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/d18470b45d21b4734187c1f639784a4e75924ed212e3fa4c7a214d19eaeb6022.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}{[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y})]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{3}y}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[\frac{\pi }{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\text{d}z]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\pi }{3}[z]_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\pi }{3}({e}^{y}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}[{e}^{y}-y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}(e-1-1+0) \\  & =\frac{\pi (e-2)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Evaluate ∫1e∫ln⁡z1∫03yyx2+y2dxdydz.

Hint: First change the order of integration to dxdzdy.

a
2π
b
π(e−2)3
c
4e
d
2πe3
e
πe+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)yx2+y2dxdzdy.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type II region as follows: R={(x,y,z):1≤z≤e,ln⁡z≤y≤1,0≤x≤3y}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before: ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫03yyx2+y2dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is type II region in the yz-plane: D={(y,z):1≤z≤e,ln⁡z≤y≤1}.

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region D is z=1 and the top boundary of the region D, written in the form z=z(y), is y=ln⁡z⟹z=ey.

Then, the type I representation of the region is D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,1≤z≤ey},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫1e∫ln⁡z1∫03yyx2+y2dxdydz=∫01∫1ey∫03yyx2+y2dxdzdy=∫01∫1ey[∫03yyx2+y2dx]dzdy=∫01∫1ey[arctan⁡(xy)]x=0x=3ydzdy=∫01∫1eyarctan⁡3dzdy=∫01∫1eyπ3dzdy=∫01[π3∫1eydz]dy=∫01π3[z]1eydy=∫01π3(ey−1)dy=π3[ey−y]01=π3(e−1−1+0)=π(e−2)3.
